title: Measures of Central Tendency Selection
description: Decision framework for selecting Mean, Median, or Mode as the authoritative summary metric.
conditions: Reporting summary baseline statistics for a feature or population metric
Data exhibits varying degrees of skewness, kurtosis, or boundary constraints
recommended_methods: Arithmetic Mean for symmetric, unskewed, unbounded Gaussian distributions
Median for skewed distributions, ordinal ranks, or datasets with severe outliers
Trimmed Mean (5% or 10% trim) for moderately skewed distributions with extreme tails
Mode for nominal categorical features and discrete count spikes
selection_rules: If absolute Fisher-Pearson skewness > 1.0, report Median as primary central tendency
If distribution is symmetric (|skewness| < 0.5) and no severe outliers, report Mean and Standard Deviation
If reporting financial, duration, or medical cost metrics, always include Median alongside Mean
limitations: Arithmetic mean is corrupted by a single arbitrarily large outlier
Median does not reflect shifts in the extreme tails of the distribution
